ticket.description:
# KS-864 (F-1009-1 + F-1009-2 only) — Wednesday's task for Ornith, VITEST, **TEST-ONLY MODE, MODIFY THE EXISTING TEST IN PLACE**

Written 2026-09-17 from origin develop `d067725ff1c7f036dbf0f726b9bf12f4daefebe7` (#1009 merged, 03:34). The test file to
modify (`ks864c-portal-env-vars.test.ts`, 80 lines, blob `f886bdadf`, the #1009 gate's equality target) was read whole.
`routes/system-status.ts` (582 lines, blob `956083916`) was read at `:40-50`, `:223-251` and `:387-471`.
**PRE-MEASURED** in a scratch clone at the tip; see `## Premises (measured)`. **This is a PARTIAL of KS-864:** it closes
only the two Polish items the #1009 gate found in its own test file. KS-864 stays open.

## THE MODE — read this twice

TEST-ONLY, MODIFY IN PLACE. Your diff contains EXACTLY ONE file: the EXISTING test file
`Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/__tests__/ks864c-portal-env-vars.test.ts`, with the ordinary header
`--- a/Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/__tests__/ks864c-portal-env-vars.test.ts` /
`+++ b/Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/__tests__/ks864c-portal-env-vars.test.ts`.
**No hunk for `system-status.ts`.** Do NOT create a new test file. Do NOT use `--- /dev/null`. Do NOT copy or modify the
reference test (`ks864b-dead-estate-portals.test.ts`); ignore it. The file's full content is in files[...]: copy every
context line from it byte-for-byte. The checker plants the tamper named at the bottom into a clone of `system-status.ts`
and expects the 🔴 F-1009-2 cell RED, then expects every cell GREEN at the untouched tip.

## What is wrong (one paragraph)

The #1009 gate measured two gaps in this file. **F-1009-1:** both blocks (`staging` and `development`) set the SAME three
portal values, so the development block cannot tell a fresh module from the one loaded under staging: deleting
`vi.resetModules();` reds 0 cells, and it also hides a development-only regression (the gate's Q-dev reds 1 cell; with the
reset removed it reds 0). **F-1009-2:** nothing checks that the block's `NODE_ENV` really reached the code: deleting
`process.env.NODE_ENV = nodeEnv;` reds 0 cells. **This task:** each block sets and expects its OWN values
(`p.value + '/' + nodeEnv`), and each block gains two cells that read the served body's `environment.env`
(`system-status.ts:437`): a 🔴 cell asserting it equals the block's `nodeEnv`, and a 🟢 control asserting it is served.
The three existing portal cells keep their titles.

## Where (no product site changes — this list is informational; every line below STAYS)

- `:228` — (correct) `url: process.env.ISSUER_PORTAL_URL || 'http://issuer-frontend:80',` — read when the module loads. Stays.
- `:237` — (correct) the verifier twin of `:228`. Stays.
- `:246` — (correct) the admin twin of `:228`. Stays.
- `:437` — (correct) `env: process.env.NODE_ENV || 'development',` — read per request; the new cells read it. The tamper replaces this line. Stays.

## The exact change — TWO hunks in the TEST file, in this order, nothing else

The lines starting with ONE SPACE are context: copy them from the file, keep them as context, never mark them `+`.
Every `+` line is byte-exact: copy it, do not paraphrase the comments, do not re-indent, do not rename `envBody` or
`controlBody`. The new cell titles are template literals in BACKTICKS, like the existing title. There is no backslash
anywhere in these lines.

E1 — inside `beforeAll`, line 57 (the portal env loop) is replaced by a comment and the loop with per-block values (2 lines):
```
@@ -54,7 +54,8 @@
       vi.resetModules();
       vi.stubGlobal('fetch', vi.fn(async () => { throw new Error('offline in test'); }));
       process.env.NODE_ENV = nodeEnv;
-      for (const p of PORTALS) process.env[p.envVar] = p.value;
+      // F-1009-1: each block sets its OWN values, so a development block that reads a staging-loaded module reds.
+      for (const p of PORTALS) process.env[p.envVar] = p.value + '/' + nodeEnv;
       const router = (await import('../routes/system-status')).default;
       const app = express();
       app.use('/api/system', router);
```

E2 — line 73 (the portal cell's `expect`) expects the same per-block value, and after line 75 (the `    }` that closes the
`for` loop), before line 76 (the `  });` that closes the `describe`), insert the two new cells (10 lines, the first blank):
```
@@ -70,8 +71,18 @@
 
     for (const p of PORTALS) {
       it(`🔴 KS-864 — ${p.name} reports ${p.envVar} under NODE_ENV=${nodeEnv}`, async () => {
-        expect((await portalUrls(port))[p.name]).toBe(p.value);
+        expect((await portalUrls(port))[p.name]).toBe(p.value + '/' + nodeEnv);
       });
     }
+
+    it(`🔴 KS-864 F-1009-2 — the served environment.env equals NODE_ENV=${nodeEnv}`, async () => {
+      const envBody = await getJson(port, '/api/system/status');
+      expect(envBody.environment.env, 'F-1009-2: the block NODE_ENV reached the route').toBe(nodeEnv);
+    });
+
+    it(`🟢 KS-864 control — the status body under NODE_ENV=${nodeEnv} carries an environment block`, async () => {
+      const controlBody = await getJson(port, '/api/system/status');
+      expect(typeof controlBody.environment.env, 'control: environment.env is served').toBe('string');
+    });
   });
 }
```

That is 13 `+` lines and 2 `-` lines. Every other line of the file (the docblock, the imports, `PORTALS`, `getJson`,
`portalUrls`, `afterAll`, the two `describeUnder(...)` calls) stays byte-identical.

Why each cell is what it is, after the edit:
- **🔴 KS-864 F-1009-2 (staging and development)** at the tip: `beforeAll` sets `NODE_ENV` to the block's value and the
  route reads it per request (`:437`), so the body says `staging` / `development`. Under the tamper `:437` always says
  `development`, so the STAGING twin fails **by assertion** (`expected 'development' to be 'staging'`); the development
  twin stays green. If the `NODE_ENV` assignment is deleted, both twins red (the runner's `test`).
- **🟢 KS-864 control (both blocks)**: green at the tip AND under the tamper; it proves the route answered with an
  `environment` block, so the 🔴 red is about the value, not a missing body.
- **The six portal cells** stay green at the tip and under this tamper. With per-block values, deleting
  `vi.resetModules();` reds the three development cells (the development block would read the staging-loaded module).

## Red cells

- 🔴 KS-864 F-1009-2 — the served environment.env equals NODE_ENV=

## Tamper (test-only mode — the checker plants this in a clone to prove your cells can go red)

line: 437
from: `    env: process.env.NODE_ENV || 'development',`
to: `    env: 'development',`
statement_ok: the `from` line is one property of the object literal `environment` at `:432-441`; every other property (`:433-436`, `:438-440`) is a separate key, so none of them can write or veto `env`, and `:441` only closes the literal. `environment` is served whole at `:467` (`res.json({ … environment, … })`). The handler runs per request, so the tamper is read by every request after the module loads; `to` makes `env` the constant `'development'` whatever `NODE_ENV` is.

## Output

Exactly ONE ```diff block containing ONLY the modified test file (`--- a/…` / `+++ b/…`, path repo-relative
`Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/__tests__/ks864c-portal-env-vars.test.ts`); the TWO hunks exactly as the headers
above say; blank context lines keep their leading space; correct hunk counts. No hunk for `system-status.ts`.

## Premises (measured)

(`f1009_pm.ToJagl`, 03:44:33–03:46:21) and round 2 (`f1009_pm.MXfA1a`, 03:46:48–03:48:29) ran the same script
(`scratchpad/f1009/premeasure.sh`, outputs `premeasure.r1.out` / `premeasure.r2.out`) at `d067725ff`. The numbers are round
2's. Round 1 differed in ONE place, the E2 header (see P11). **Every vitest, tsc and checker run was wrapped in
`sandbox-exec` with off-host outbound denied (loopback allowed).** The file's harness is loopback-only (`fetch` stubbed to
throw), and no baseline red appeared.

- **P1 tip.** origin develop = `d067725ff1c7f036dbf0f726b9bf12f4daefebe7` (#1009 squash). Instruments: `git ls-remote` at 03:38:30, 03:46:48 and 03:48:35; GitHub branches API at 03:40:57. QA-3 (`process.env.NODE_ENV = nodeEnv;` deleted): **6/6 green**. Q-dev alone: 1 red (issuer development). These are the gate's rows 7, 8, 12 and 6 exactly (03:47:04–03:47:23).

Both 🟢 controls, the development twin and the six portal cells are green. Whole suite with the golden under Tenv: 404 / 403 passed / 1 failed, that same cell only (03:48:04–03:48:10).

Q-dev is NOT a discriminating tamper for F-1009-1: it reds the OLD file too (P4) and the golden 1 (03:47:29–03:48:04).

Test-side (not gradeable by a product tamper): golden with the `NODE_ENV` assignment deleted (included-program tsc rc 0): **2 red, both F-1009-2 twins, by assertion** (`expected 'test' to be 'staging'` / `… 'development'`). Open PRs: 18, and **0** touch ks864c, `system-status.ts` or `routes/verification.ts` (GitHub files API GET for every open PR, 03:40:57–03:41:22). `build_input.sh` REFUSES this ticket as-is (`attached to pull request(s)`, rc 2, 03:42:51). ## Notes for the raise (not for the model)

- **PR note: "Part of KS-864 (F-1009-1, F-1009-2)". Never "Closes" / "Fixes".** KS-864 stays open. This is a test-only follow-up to the #1009 gate's two Polish findings in its own test file.
- The checker grades **F-1009-2 only** (tamper Tenv at `:437`). **F-1009-1 is NOT GRADED BY THE CHECKER.** Its property is the test's own `vi.resetModules()`, so no product-line tamper reds its removal. It is graded by P8: the reset deleted reds the 3 development cells, and the Tlatch proxy reds 1 cell on the golden and 0 on the old file. F-1009-2's setup half (the `NODE_ENV` assignment) is graded by P9 (2 reds).
- Tamper choice, measured: the gate's Q-dev does NOT discriminate. It reds the OLD file too (1 cell), so it cannot show the new cells add anything (P4, P8).
- **Harness: `build_input.sh` refuses KS-864** because the ticket carries PR attachments (#1007, #1009, both merged). There is no override for that gate. `night/inputs/code_864_f1009.json` was built by `scratchpad/f1009/build_input.prgate-off.sh`, a copy whose `diff` against the real builder is ONE line (`refuse(f"attached to pull request(s)…")` → `print(…)`). A queue line must therefore carry `input=` (the runner honours a pre-built input). A plain `KS-864-F1009` line with pins would be BUILD_REFUSED.
- **Harness: never queue this as bare `KS-864`.** `night/briefs/KS-864.md` is an OLDER brief, and the builder would read it as the prompt. The input was built under the id `KS-864-F1009` (the builder's `int(split("-")[1])` reads 864), so the brief read is `KS-864-F1009.md`.
- Builder pins used (all required): `product=Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/system-status.ts ref=services/api-gateway/src/__tests__/ks864b-dead-estate-portals.test.ts test_file=services/api-gateway/src/__tests__/ks864c-portal-env-vars.test.ts line=437 ctx=65536`, with `NIGHT_BRIEFS_DIR` = the directory holding this brief. Without `test_file=` the model gets no file content to copy context from. The input is ~11.7K prompt tokens (builder estimate, 03:50:36), well inside ctx 65536.
- The two `+  });`-shaped closing lines (`    });`) also exist at the tip. They are structural closers of the new cells, not re-added anchors, and A3d ignores lines under 8 chars.
